verifier_note: All factual checks below were executed. Scratch scripts live in /tmp/t07/ (indep.py, posctl.py, detail.py, detail2.py, prob.py, exh.py, exh2.py). Snapshot was read-only; nothing in /home/rohit/sprs-review/snapshot was modified.

positive_control_independent_check.evidence: I re-derived the positive control from scratch, twice, without importing the orchestrator's script. (1) LEAF-GENERATOR SANITY CHECK AGAINST TABLE V: /tmp/t07/indep.py reimplements the leaf formula L[i]=(i+1)*1000.0+((37i+13) mod 100)/100+0.007 (snapshot/src/sprs_core.py:5368, make_leaf_val, op=0b111) and the canonical heap-indexed FBT (leaves at heap indices N-1..2N-2 ascending, node n has children 2n+1,2n+2 -- CBTree, sprs_core.py:381-399), using plain Python FP64 addition. It reproduces ALL SIXTEEN roots of paper/tables/invariance.tex EXACTLY: N=8 0x40E1948E978D4FDF ... N=8192 0x421F40FA40427EFA, 16/16 MATCH. (2) CROSS-CHECK VIA THE PROJECT'S OWN BIT-EXACT ADDER: importing sprs_core and running the emitter's own oracle loop (CBTree(N).postorder() + _fp64_add_bits) gives the same roots (N=8, 200, 8192 checked). So the reconstruction is validated three independent ways. (3) REORDERING: I compared the canonical root against left-to-right sequential, right-to-left sequential, adjacent-pairwise (recursive doubling), block-ring at G in {2..128}, block-recursive-doubling at the same G, 20 random association trees, and 20 random leaf permutations, per N. REORDERING DOES CHANGE THE ROOT. My max-ulp figures match the orchestrator's EXACTLY at N=512 (5), 1500 (9), 3000 (16), 4096 (27) and 8192 (55); the 55-ulp figure at N=8192 comes specifically from right-to-left sequential summation. Left-to-right sequential differs from canonical at 10 of my 16 N. I therefore CONFIRM the orchestrator's headline verdict (CONFIRMED_NARROWER: the oracle is not vacuous, but discriminating power is weak and non-monotone in N). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE ORCHESTRATOR'S CELL VALUES, both minor and both in the direction of making the numbers less fragile: (a) its 'random_differing' counts are 20-sample estimates and are seed-noise; its '0/20 at N=16' is not robust -- I measured the underlying probability with 1000 samples per N (/tmp/t07/prob.py) and get P(a uniformly random association order differs from canonical) = 0.16 at N=8, 0.13 at N=16, 0.90 at N=1024, 0.08 at N=1500, 0.11 at N=3000, 0.29 at N=8192 -- low everywhere, but never zero and NOT monotone in N. (b) it tested N=1000, which is not a row of Table V; the corresponding table row is N=1024 (max_ulp 6, not 7). Neither correction changes the verdict. I additionally settled the question EXACTLY rather than by sampling at small N: exhaustive enumeration of all 40,320 leaf permutations under FBT(8) yields only THREE distinct 64-bit roots, of which 35,712 (88.571%) equal the canonical one, so P(detect a random leaf-order violation at N=8) = 0.1143; exhaustive interval-DP over all in-order binary tree shapes gives 3 distinct roots over 429 shapes at N=8 (P(==canonical)=0.825) and 4 distinct roots spanning -2..+1 ulp over all 9,694,845 shapes at N=16 (P(==canonical)=0.656).

verdicts.finding: No positive control that a non-canonical reduction order would change the result on the campaign's leaf vector; at N=8 every alternative order the reviewer tested gives the identical 64-bit root.
verdicts.observed: Reviewer r04's numbers reproduce EXACTLY. /tmp/t07/detail.py, using the reviewer's own order set (sequential, pairwise, block-ring at each G<=N power of two, block-recursive-doubling at each G<=N): N=8 -> 0 of 8 differ; N=16 -> 2 of 10; N=32 -> 2 of 12; N=128 -> 5 of 16; /tmp/t07/detail2.py: N=4096 -> 17 of 26. The reviewer's quoted hex is also exact: canonical N=1024 = 0x41BF47D2026872B1, ring at G=64 = 0x41BF47D2026872AE (3 ulp). The only order in my wider set that differs at N=8 is right-to-left sequential (0x40E1948E978D4FDE, 1 ulp), which the reviewer did not test. Exhaustively (/tmp/t07/exh.py, /tmp/t07/exh2.py): over ALL 40,320 leaf permutations at N=8 only 3 distinct roots occur and 88.57% equal canonical; over ALL 429 in-order tree shapes at N=8, 3 roots, 82.5% canonical; over ALL 9,694,845 shapes at N=16, 4 roots spanning -2..+1 ulp, 65.6% canonical. Paper main.tex:2047-2049 already concedes the phenomenon ('We deliberately do not claim that reordering always changes the result. It does not') but reports no number.
verdicts.what_is_true: Alternative reduction orders DO change the 64-bit root on the campaign's own leaf vector -- so the oracle is not vacuous -- but the probability that a given reordering is detected is low and strongly N-dependent: 0.11 at N=8, 0.13 at N=16, up to 0.90 at N=1024, back down to 0.08 at N=1500. The maximum divergence ever observed is 55 ulp (right-to-left sequential at N=8192); a typical random reassociation moves the root by 1-3 ulp or not at all. In particular a standard adjacent-pairwise/recursive-doubling reduction produces the bit-identical canonical root at 13 of the 16 tested N.
verdicts.consequence: The evaluation is NOT invalidated -- no re-run of the RTL campaign is needed. But the paper cannot present all sixteen rows of Table V as equally strong evidence, and it must not imply that a competitor's reduction order would have been caught. The cheapest adequate fix is a claim narrowing plus one measured column: report per-N the measured order-sensitivity (P(random reassociation differs), and 'differs / total' over a fixed enumerated order set), computed by a ~30-line pure-Python script with no RTL. That converts the admitted weakness at main.tex:2047-2049 from a concession into a measurement, and it is the single highest-value paragraph available for the page cost.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: This is the finding a hostile referee will run themselves in ten minutes. It reproduces exactly. Leaving it unaddressed is the largest single first-turn rejection risk in this theme.

verdicts.finding: The mutation campaign is under-powered and mis-targeted: 20 of 39 instances, one fixed (alpha,mu) per instance, and address-substitution mutants that most likely trigger a watchdog hang rather than an oracle root mismatch.
verdicts.observed: COVERAGE, confirmed: experiments/mutation/_mutation_runner.py:108-132 hard-codes TARGETS = 20 (instance, N, G) triples, one per leaf-count class, with the source comment 'within each class we take the smallest G'; :305-308 picks base = sorted(tbs)[0], i.e. ONE testbench image per instance chosen alphabetically. Recomputed from results/mutation/mutation_results.json: 20 instances, 20 distinct TB images, S2 stage = '2a' for 20 of 20, S3 stage = '3a' for 18 of 20 ('3e' for the other two); against 39 HW-validated instances and 2,822 passing configurations in results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv. SEED CORRELATION, confirmed and worse than stated: only three seeds (1000,1001,1002) are used across all 20 instances (:314), so the 54 addr_sub mutants draw their target address from just NINE distinct values {7:1, 27:2, 28:12, 38:1, 39:12, 43:6, 49:6, 53:1, 60:13}. HANG-VS-MISMATCH: the mechanism is real and I proved it for a subset. rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:513-521 stalls the DE stage whenever a COMPUTE reads a DMEM address with scoreboard bit 0; :776-786 the watchdog counts cycles with nothing retiring and :818/:844 force P_ERROR at WATCHDOG_MAX=20000, so all_done never asserts and the TB takes its 'TIMEOUT' branch (sprs_core.py:5576-5577), not its root-comparison branch (:5578). sprs_core.py:5102-5135 (DMEMAllocator) allocates addresses densely from 1 upward, incrementing peak_local at most once per node and once per landed remote child, so no PE can ever write a DMEM address above 2N-1. Comparing that bound against the recorded targets: 11 of 54 addr_sub mutants -- all six at N=8, all three at N=10, two of three at N=16 -- provably repoint addr_a at an address that NO PE in that instance can ever write, so those mutants provably could not have been detected by a root mismatch. For the remaining 43 the answer cannot be settled from the artifact: the emitted TB images are not in the snapshot (find . -name 'tb_*' returns 0 files) and the runner deletes the xsim log (shutil.rmtree in the finally block, :283). DOCUMENTATION CONFLICT, confirmed: main.tex:1170-1171 says 'replace addr_b with the DMEM address of a different tree node'; main.tex:2093-2095 says 'repoint addr_a at a different DMEM address'; the code and the data match the second, weaker version.
verdicts.what_is_true: The campaign is 20 instances x 1 compiler image x 2 classes x 3 seeds, with only 3 independent RNG draws, all at the smallest G in each class. At least 11 of the 54 address-substitution mutants provably cannot have been detected by a root mismatch and must have been detected by the fail-stop/timeout path. The paper's two descriptions of the address-substitution mutation contradict each other, and the implemented one is the weaker.
verdicts.consequence: Two cheap fixes, no new RTL runs. (1) Fix main.tex:1170-1171 to match the implementation (addr_a, arbitrary DMEM address) -- a one-line edit that removes a self-contradiction any RTL-reading referee will find. (2) Disclose in the Table V caption that mutation cells come from one TB image per instance at the smallest G, three seeds, and that address-substitution detection includes fail-stop-by-stall as well as root mismatch. A re-run with live-node targets would be nicer but is not required to survive review IF the claim is narrowed to 'the harness refuses to certify' rather than 'the oracle flags divergence'.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Moderate. The self-contradicting mutation description is the sharp edge; the coverage thinness is survivable if disclosed.

verdicts.finding: The oracle and the stimulus share the same leaf enumeration, so an error in the canonical leaf enumeration is undetectable by the harness.
verdicts.observed: Verified by reading src/sprs_core.py:5461-5462, which computes 'leaf_list = tree.leaves(); leaf_to_global_idx = {leaf: idx for idx, leaf in enumerate(leaf_list)}' ONCE. The oracle then uses it at :5473-5475 ('gidx = leaf_to_global_idx.get(node, 0); _, bits = make_leaf_val(gidx, alu_op)') and the GCI stimulus uses the SAME dict at :5547-5549 ('global_idx = leaf_to_global_idx.get(node, 0); _, val_64 = make_leaf_val(global_idx, alu_op); load_gci(...)'). experiments/mutation/_mutation_runner.py:84 rebuilds the identical map, so the mutation harness inherits the blind spot. A permuted leaf enumeration therefore moves EXPECTED and the GCI contents together and the TB still reports [PASS]. I additionally quantified how much power an INDEPENDENT oracle would have had: computing the root under heap-index enumeration versus visual (left-to-right / in-order) enumeration for every non-power-of-two N in the suite, the two differ at ONLY ONE of the sixteen N -- N=200, 0x41732B4046666667 vs 0x41732B4046666666, exactly one ulp, which is precisely the example the paper itself cites in Sec 3.1. At N=10, 50, 100, 500, 1500 and 3000 the two enumerations give bit-identical roots.
verdicts.what_is_true: The harness structurally cannot detect a leaf-enumeration error, because one dictionary feeds both the expected value and the stimulus. Separately, even an independent oracle would detect the heap-vs-visual enumeration difference at only 1 of the 16 evaluated N.
verdicts.consequence: Do NOT add the mutation class the reviewer asks for. It would fire at exactly one N (200) and be silent at the other fifteen, so it would cost a re-run and buy a one-row result. The correct and far cheaper fix is a one-sentence scope statement: Claim 1 is conditional on the leaf enumeration being the ABI's heap order, C-leaf is asserted by code inspection and not by dynamic check, and the harness does not test it. That is exactly the kind of honest scoping Q1 referees reward. Optionally add the measured fact -- the heap/visual roots coincide at 15 of 16 N -- as a single clause, since it is a genuinely interesting statement about how weak this class of bug is.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Low-moderate. Only an RTL-reading referee finds it, but when found it looks like a hidden circularity unless pre-empted.

verdicts.finding: Mutation 'detection' is defined as the absence of [PASS], conflating an oracle-observed divergence with a non-terminating simulation, and the released record does not distinguish them.
verdicts.observed: TRUE OF THE MUTATION CAMPAIGN. experiments/mutation/_mutation_runner.py:257-262: 'if "[PASS]" in txt: out["detected"]=False; elif "[FAIL]" in txt or "TIMEOUT" in txt: out["detected"]=True', and :263-266 maps a Python-level subprocess timeout to detected=True as well. results/mutation/mutation_results.json carries only the keys [G, N, detected, error, instance, kind, mutation, seed, tb]; there is no verdict-kind field, and the xsim stdout is destroyed by shutil.rmtree in the finally block, so it cannot be recovered without re-running. Of the 108 records, 107 have detected=true with error='' and one has detected=null / 'no verdict in xsim output'; none took the TimeoutExpired branch, but in-simulation TIMEOUT and in-simulation root mismatch are indistinguishable in the released data. BUT FALSE OF THE MAIN CAMPAIGN, which is what Table V's zero-divergence column rests on: experiments/phase1/_bypass_runner.py:130-139 assigns three DISTINCT error codes -- OK_BYPASS on [PASS], SIM_TB_TIMEOUT_BYPASS on TIMEOUT, SIM_FAIL_BYPASS on [FAIL] without TIMEOUT -- and preserves the failing line in the Error column. Recomputed over all three released HW CSVs (2,844 + 2,854 + 5 rows): 2,822 pass; 22 (unified) / 32 (maxpe) / 5 (maxp_mod_fat) fail; every single failure is SIM_TB_TIMEOUT_BYPASS or SIM_WALLCLOCK_TIMEOUT_BYPASS; the string 'root_result' appears ZERO times in any Error field and SIM_FAIL_BYPASS occurs ZERO times. So no configuration in the entire released campaign ever produced a wrong-but-finite root.
verdicts.what_is_true: The conflation is real, but it is confined to the 108-mutant campaign. The 2,822-configuration invariance campaign does record the distinction and shows zero root mismatches and 22-32 timeouts. Separately confirmed: mutate_addr_sub (:143-159) is the only mutator not validated against the software oracle before injection, whereas mutate_leaf_corrupt (:171-190) escalates the flipped bit until the software oracle confirms the canonical root moved.
verdicts.consequence: Cheapest adequate fix is disclosure, not re-running. Add to the Table V caption or Sec 7.2 that 'detected' means the harness refused to certify -- root mismatch OR fail-stop -- and that the two are not separated in the released record; and state the main-campaign fact that all 22 non-passing configurations failed by simulation timeout, none by root mismatch. That second sentence is a genuine strengthening the paper currently leaves on the table, and it is free: the number is already in the released CSV.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Moderate. 'Detection means absence of PASS' is quotable and looks like measurement laundering unless the main-campaign distinction is stated.

verdicts.finding: The one executed check is weakly powered against reassociation on the campaign's own leaf vector, and mutation testing cannot establish otherwise because mutants are selected for detectability.
verdicts.observed: r12's headline computations reproduce, several to the digit. (a) EXACT MATCH: exhaustive over all 40,320 leaf permutations at N=8 under FBT(8) I get exactly 3 distinct roots with 35,712 (88.571%) canonical, i.e. P(detect)=0.1143 -- r12 said 3 roots, 35,712/40,320, 0.114 (/tmp/t07/exh.py). (b) SUBSTANTIVELY CONFIRMED, one number wrong: exhaustive interval-DP over all in-order tree shapes gives 3 distinct roots at N=8 over 429 shapes and 4 distinct roots spanning -2..+1 ulp at N=16 -- r12's roots/ulp spans are right, but the N=16 shape count is 9,694,845 (Catalan C_15), not the 742,900 (C_13) they state (/tmp/t07/exh2.py). (c)(d) CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE: adjacent-pairwise recursive doubling reproduces the canonical root bit-for-bit at 13 of my 16 tested N, and a block-ring reduction matches at some G at every N I tested. (e) CONFIRMED: my 1000-sample-per-N estimate gives P(random association differs) in [0.08, 0.90]; r12 said P(equal) in [0.12, 0.91]. (f) CONFIRMED EXACTLY, and this is the strongest part of the finding: instrumenting the canonical evaluation across all sixteen N, of 21,400 FADD operations, the count of operands that are negative / zero / subnormal / Inf / NaN is 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0, and effective subtraction occurs 0 times. SELECTION-FOR-DETECTABILITY CONFIRMED for leaf_corrupt (_mutation_runner.py:179-187 escalates the bit index until oracle_root changes) but NOT for addr_sub, which does no such check. ONE r12 CLAIM REFUTED: 'nothing is ever absorbed and no cancellation ever occurs' is wrong as to absorption -- 491 of 1,229 FADDs at N in {8,200,1024} are inexact (they round), and the paper's own escalation data (recorded bit indices 0-14 in the released JSON) is direct evidence of absorption. Cancellation, however, genuinely never occurs.
verdicts.what_is_true: The leaf vector is all-positive normals of a single narrow character. It exercises exactly one of the six documented FADD rules. Detection probability against a random reassociation is 0.11-0.35 at N<=16 and never exceeds ~0.90 at any N. Half the mutation campaign (leaf_corrupt) is conditioned on detectability by construction. No reassociation mutant exists in either class.
verdicts.consequence: Two of the sentences r12 quotes are over-claims and should be narrowed, at zero page cost: main.tex:2043-2045 ('reassociation is observable in the low-order bits') should read 'reassociation is observable in the low-order bits at most, but not all, N -- we measure this in Table V'; and the appendix's 'reassociation is therefore observable' should be cut. Do NOT add adversarial leaf vectors as a new experiment unless a referee demands it: the acceptance gain is small relative to the cost, and the same rhetorical work is done for free by reporting the measured order-sensitivity from D040. DO state explicitly, as a limitation, that the FTZ, signed-zero, NaN and Inf rules of the FADD policy are specified but not exercised by any of the 2,822 configurations -- see D109, where I confirm this exactly.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: High. r12 is the adversarial reviewer and the computations are correct and cheap to redo. The over-claim sentences are the vulnerable surface, not the underlying result.

verdicts.finding: Mutation coverage is thin where the claim is weakest, and Property 2 has none.
verdicts.observed: experiments/mutation/_mutation_runner.py:191 'MUTATORS = {"addr_sub": mutate_addr_sub, "leaf_corrupt": mutate_leaf_corrupt}' -- exactly two classes, both compiler-side (they mutate the emitted testbench text, not the RTL). No fault is ever injected against F-misroute, F-arb, F-credit or F-watchdog, so Property 2's fail-stop subtree has no direct mutation evidence. NARROWER, in the paper's favour: at least 11 of the 54 addr_sub mutants provably drive a COMPUTE to read a never-written DMEM address (see D045), which forces exactly the F-sb-gate -> watchdog -> P_ERROR fail-stop path at rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:513-521 and :818/:844. So the fail-stop path IS exercised, incidentally, by 11+ mutants -- the paper simply does not say so because the harness does not record the verdict kind.
verdicts.what_is_true: There is no mutation class aimed at the fabric invariants, but the scoreboard-gate/watchdog fail-stop path is in fact exercised by a provable subset of the existing address-substitution mutants.
verdicts.consequence: Do not add a fabric fault-injection campaign. Instead recover the credit already earned: state that address substitution to an unallocated DMEM address exercises F-sb-gate and F-watchdog, and that these mutants fail-stop rather than certifying. That is an ADD ANALYSIS on data already in hand (the recorded target addresses plus the 2N-1 allocator bound) and needs no simulation. Narrow Property 2's evidentiary claim to 'argued, plus incidentally exercised' rather than 'tested'.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Low. This is an editor-scope nicety, not a rejection driver.

verdicts.finding: A single leaf vector per N, and five of the six documented FADD rules are never exercised at system level.
verdicts.observed: The leaf vector is a deterministic function of the index alone (sprs_core.py:5366-5370), so there is exactly one leaf vector per N by construction. For the FADD rules I instrumented the canonical evaluation over all sixteen N and counted operand classes across all 21,400 FADD operations: negative operands 0, zero operands 0, subnormal operands 0, Inf operands 0, NaN operands 0, effective-subtraction events 0. Root magnitudes span 3.6e4 to 3.36e10, all positive normals. Against the six rules enumerated at main.tex:1073-1097: rule 1 (input FTZ) 0 activations, rule 2 (RNE) exercised heavily -- 491 of 1,229 FADDs at N in {8,200,1024} are inexact -- rule 3 (output FTZ) 0, rule 4 (signed-zero cancellation) 0, rule 5 (NaN propagation) 0, rule 6 (infinity arithmetic) 0. Exactly five of six unexercised, as stated.
verdicts.what_is_true: Of the six FADD-policy rules the paper specifies as the deterministic contract, only round-to-nearest-even is exercised by any of the 2,822 RTL-validated configurations. The other five -- input FTZ, output FTZ, signed-zero cancellation, NaN propagation, infinity arithmetic -- have zero dynamic coverage at system level.
verdicts.consequence: This is the cheapest high-value fix in the whole theme and it is a CLARIFY LIMITATION, not an experiment. One sentence in Sec 8 (limitations, near the existing L4 'FTZ+RNE subset' entry at main.tex:2773): 'Rules 1 and 3-6 of the FADD policy are specified and implemented but are not exercised by any configuration in the campaign; the evaluated leaf vector consists entirely of positive normals, and all 21,400 system-level FADDs take the normal+normal path.' Stating it pre-empts the reviewer; being caught not stating it is what costs a round. If any new experiment in this theme is worth its cost it is this one -- a single N=128 run with a leaf vector seeded with +/-0, +/-Inf, NaN and subnormals -- but it is NOT required for acceptance once the limitation is disclosed, because Claim 1 is explicitly a statement about determinism of a pure function, not about IEEE conformance.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Moderate-high if undisclosed, near-zero if disclosed. A referee who checks will find it in five minutes and will read silence as concealment.

verdicts.finding: The 107/107 leaf-corruption detection rate is true by construction of the mutation protocol and carries little information.
verdicts.observed: _mutation_runner.py:179-187 escalates the flipped bit position from the mantissa LSB upward until 'oracle_root(N, cand) != base_root', so every counted leaf_corrupt mutant is guaranteed by construction to move the canonical root. The escalation depths actually reached, recovered from the released JSON, are bits {0:4, 1:2, 2:1, 3:6, 4:3, 5:5, 6:8, 7:5, 8:1, 9:7, 10:5, 11:4, 14:3} -- median bit 6, i.e. the naive LSB mutator would have been absorbed most of the time, exactly as the paper says. I independently confirmed the paper's own absorption-depth example at main.tex:2233-2235 ('for N=8 the smallest root-changing flip is bit 5 on L_0, bit 4 on L_1, bit 3 on L_2'): recomputed as bit 5 on L0, bit 4 on L1, bit 3 on L2 -- exact. NARROWER: it is NOT true by construction that the testbench then reports FAIL. A vacuous oracle (one comparing nothing, or comparing against a value derived from the run) would report PASS on all 54. So the 54/54 leaf_corrupt result does carry the one bit of information it is advertised to carry -- the oracle is not vacuous -- but carries no information about detection probability against realistic faults, and pooling it with the 53 addr_sub results into a single '107/107' headline is what makes the number look stronger than it is.
verdicts.what_is_true: The leaf-corruption class is constructed so the root must move; its 54/54 result establishes non-vacuity of the bit comparison and nothing more. The pooled 107/107 figure mixes that with 53 address-substitution mutants of which at least 11 provably fail-stop rather than mismatch.
verdicts.consequence: REMOVE OR NARROW CLAIM, zero page cost, arguably negative page cost. Split the two classes wherever 107/107 currently appears (abstract, Sec 7.2 'the oracle flagged all 107', conclusion) and say what each establishes: leaf corruption -> the comparison is live; address substitution -> the harness refuses to certify. Reporting the naive pre-escalation absorption rate as the paper's Sec 7.2 already gestures at would be a genuinely interesting descriptive statistic, but it requires a re-run and is not needed.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Moderate. A statistics referee will flag the pooled number; the fix is free.

verdicts.finding: The PASS oracle reads the root PE's last-COMPUTE ALU latch, not the root DMEM slot that Claim 1 quantifies over.
verdicts.observed: The testbench emits, at src/sprs_core.py:5571-5578, 'if(all_done && u_sys.gen_node[<root_gpu>].u_cn.result==EXPECTED) $display("[PASS] ...")'. In rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv, 'result' is an output register (:50) updated at :804-806 (P_RUN) and :831-833 (P_DRAIN) by 'if (ex_valid && ex_advance && ex_opcode == 4'h2) result <= alu_result_comb' -- i.e. it latches the ALU output of the LAST COMPUTE retired on that PE, whatever node that was. The DMEM write is a separate action at :618-622 ('COMPUTE -- ALU result -> DMEM writeback', fsm_dmem_addr = ex_dest, fsm_dmem_data = alu_result_comb). Claim 1 (main.tex:826-828) states 'the observed 64-bit root DMEM value at program termination equals R_can'. The testbench never reads DMEM. The two quantities can diverge in at least three ways that the RTL makes explicit: (i) if the root node's COMPUTE is not the last COMPUTE retired on the root PE, the latch holds a different node's value; (ii) an inbound PIU/GCI write to the root DMEM slot after the root COMPUTE would change DMEM but not the latch -- and the design has an explicit ex_dmem_collision signal at :505-506 acknowledging that PIU/GCI and COMPUTE contend for the same DMEM port; (iii) a dropped or arbitrated-away DMEM write leaves DMEM stale while the latch is correct.
verdicts.what_is_true: Every [PASS] in the campaign certifies the root PE's final COMPUTE ALU output, not the root DMEM slot. Claim 1 as written quantifies over the DMEM slot. The checked quantity is therefore strictly a proxy for the claimed quantity, and the write-arbitration hazard the paper itself discusses in Sec 3.5 / Sec 'write-arb' is precisely a case where they could differ.
verdicts.consequence: Cheapest adequate fix is an EDIT to Claim 1, not a testbench change: restate the observable as 'the root PE's final COMPUTE result' (or 'the value the root PE computes for node 0'), and add one clause in Sec 7 noting that the harness checks the ALU output register rather than DMEM[addr_map[root][0]]. Changing the testbench to read DMEM would require re-running all 2,822 configurations for a result that will be identical -- indefensible against the cheaper option. This edit is important beyond cosmetics because it interacts with the fail-stop/Property-2 discussion: a referee who notices that Claim 1's observable is never read will discount the whole invariance table.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: Moderate-high. An RTL-reading referee who finds that the claim's own observable is never measured will treat it as a validity gap, and it is a one-sentence fix.

verdicts.finding: Oracle non-vacuity is established on 20 testbench images out of ~2,900, all at the smallest G in their leaf class and almost all from one compiler triple.
verdicts.observed: 20 TB images confirmed: _mutation_runner.py:305-308 selects sorted(tbs)[0] per instance, and the released JSON contains exactly 20 distinct (instance, tb) pairs. 'Smallest G' confirmed by the source comment at :124-128 ('within each class we take the smallest G, since elaboration cost scales with the node count and detection is a property of the oracle rather than of scale') and by the TARGETS list, e.g. N=512 uses G=8 and G=32 where Table V records six compiled (G,topology) points. 'Almost all one compiler triple' confirmed precisely: S2 algorithm = 2a for 20 of 20 instances; S3 algorithm = 3a for 18 of 20 (3e for two); S4 refinement varies (none/4g/4c2). Denominator: 2,844 attempted and 2,822 passing rows in results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv, so 20/2822 = 0.7%.
verdicts.what_is_true: Mutation evidence for oracle non-vacuity comes from 0.7% of the validated configurations, one image per leaf class, all sharing the S2 assignment algorithm and 90% sharing the S3 mapping algorithm.
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY LIMITATION only. One clause in the Table V caption stating the sampling ('each mutation cell is one testbench image per instance, at the smallest G in that class, under a single compiler triple, three seeds'). Widening the sample would cost RTL runs to learn something the paper does not claim -- non-vacuity is a property of the harness, and the harness is the same code for every image. Do not spend on it.

verdicts.issue: T07-X1 (theme question, not a docket issue): is the invariance result a measurement or a consistency check? Where do the reported roots and the divergence column come from?
verdicts.finding: Theme T07 asks whether per-run observed roots exist anywhere in the released data and how the divergence column is produced.
verdicts.observed: THE DIVERGENCE COLUMN IS A LITERAL. paper/scripts/gen_tables.py:183-185 writes each row as f'{N} & {nc} & {nv} & {ncfg} & \\texttt{{0x{root}}} & 0 & ...' -- the '0' in the Div. column is hard-coded in the format string and is never computed from data. THE ROOT COLUMN IS THE COMPILER'S OWN PREDICTION. gen_tables.py:105-120 (canonical_roots) obtains it by regex-scraping 'EXPECTED = 64'h...' out of the emitted testbench SOURCE files, not from any simulation output. THE GENERATOR'S ONE ASSERTION IS A TAUTOLOGY. gen_tables.py:157 asserts len(exps)==1, i.e. all TBs at a given N embed the same EXPECTED constant. But EXPECTED is computed at src/sprs_core.py:5461-5484 from 'tree' and 'alu_op' ALONE -- CBTree(N).postorder(), CBTree(N).leaves(), make_leaf_val -- with no dependence on topology, G, assignment, mapping, refinement or schedule. So EXPECTED is provably a function of N alone and the assertion cannot fail. NO OBSERVED ROOT IS STORED ANYWHERE. The testbench does print the observed value ('root_gpu=%0d root_result=%0d expected=%0d', sprs_core.py:5572), but experiments/phase1/_bypass_runner.py:128-139 extracts only a boolean plus per-PE cycle counters and then deletes the working directory (shutil.rmtree in the finally block at :163), and the released CSVs carry only [Instance, Pipeline, TB_Name, Pass, Cycles, SimTime_s, ErrorCode, Error]. I grepped all three CSVs: the string 'root_result' appears 0 times. THE EMPIRICAL CONTENT SURVIVES ANYWAY. Pass==True is by construction equivalent to (observed == EXPECTED(N)), and EXPECTED(N) is the same constant for every configuration at that N, so 'all passing configurations at N share one 64-bit root' is a SOUND inference from 2,822 independent RTL simulations. And the 22 non-passing configurations are all timeouts, none root mismatches (verified above under D080), so nothing is hidden in the dropped denominator.
verdicts.what_is_true: The invariance result IS a real measurement -- 2,822 RTL simulations each confirmed the fabric's root equals a constant that depends only on N -- but it is measured one run at a time against a fixed per-N constant, not by comparing recorded observed roots across configurations, and the observed roots themselves are not retained in the artifact. The 'Div.' column is a hard-coded 0 in the table generator, and the generator's only self-check (one distinct EXPECTED per N) is a software tautology that tests nothing about the compiler or the fabric.
verdicts.consequence: This is the sharpest thing in the theme and it cuts BOTH ways, so handle it with precision rather than concession. (1) Do NOT restate the result as 'a consistency check' -- that would be a false concession; the 2,822 PASS verdicts are genuine RTL measurements and a==c, b==c ==> a==b is valid. (2) DO fix the presentation so a referee cannot mistake a literal for a measurement: either compute the Div. column from the data (it is a two-line change to gen_tables.py: Div = count of rows at that N with Pass==False and ErrorCode==SIM_FAIL_BYPASS, which is 0) or relabel the column 'Root mismatches (of HW-val.)' and state in the caption that all non-passing configurations failed by simulation timeout, not by root mismatch -- with the count. The second is better: it is honest, it is free, and it converts a column that currently looks like a placeholder into a reported measurement. (3) DO drop or rephrase 'the set of observed 64-bit roots has cardinality exactly one' (main.tex:2162-2163) to 'every HW-validated configuration reproduced the same per-N canonical root', which is what was actually measured. (4) Consider retaining and releasing the observed roots on the next run; not required for acceptance, but its absence is why this question needed three hours of forensics to answer.
verdicts.cost_if_ignored: High if a referee opens gen_tables.py, which the artifact invites them to do. A hard-coded 0 in the primary results table of a determinism paper is the single most damaging thing an artifact-evaluating referee could find, even though the underlying result is sound.

headline: I independently confirm the positive control and, at several points, reproduce the reviewers' numbers to the digit. Reconstructing the leaf generator and canonical FBT from scratch reproduces all sixteen Table V roots exactly, which validates the reconstruction; reordering then genuinely does move the 64-bit root (up to 55 ulp at N=8192, via right-to-left sequential summation), so the oracle is not vacuous and no re-run of the RTL campaign is required. But the discriminating power is low and non-monotone in N: exhaustively, all 40,320 leaf permutations at N=8 yield only three distinct roots with 88.57% canonical (P(detect)=0.114), all 429 in-order tree shapes at N=8 yield three roots and all 9,694,845 shapes at N=16 yield four spanning two ulp, and a 1000-sample estimate puts P(a random reassociation is detected) between 0.08 and 0.90 across the sixteen N. Reviewer r04's N=8/16/32/128/4096 counts and even their N=1024 ring-at-G=64 hex reproduce exactly, as do r12's N=8 permutation figures. Of ten docket issues, six are CONFIRMED and four CONFIRMED_NARROWER; nothing in T07 is refuted, though two of r12's supporting numbers are wrong (the N=16 tree-shape count, and the assertion that nothing is ever absorbed -- 491 of 1,229 FADDs actually round). The single most consequential verdict is the theme's own question, T07-X1: the 'Div.' column of the primary results table is a hard-coded literal '0' in paper/scripts/gen_tables.py:184, the '64-bit root result' column is regex-scraped out of the testbench SOURCE rather than any simulation output, the generator's only self-check (one distinct EXPECTED per N) is a tautology because EXPECTED provably depends on N alone, and no observed root is retained anywhere in the released artifact. The underlying result nevertheless survives -- Pass==True is equivalent to observed==EXPECTED(N), 2,822 configurations passed, and all 22 failures are simulation timeouts with zero root mismatches anywhere in the released CSVs -- so the fix is presentational and free: compute or relabel the divergence column and report the timeouts-not-mismatches fact, which is a strengthening the paper currently leaves unused. Alongside it, three near-free edits carry most of the remaining acceptance risk: restate Claim 1's observable as the root PE's final COMPUTE result rather than the root DMEM slot (the testbench reads the ALU latch at btree_fsm_fast.sv:806, never DMEM); disclose that five of the six documented FADD rules are exercised by exactly zero of the 21,400 system-level FADDs; and split the pooled 107/107 mutation figure, since its leaf-corruption half is constructed to move the root and at least 11 of its 53 address-substitution mutants provably repoint an operand at a DMEM address no PE can ever write, so they fail-stop through the watchdog rather than through the bit comparison. Only one new experiment in this theme is even arguable -- a single adversarial leaf vector exercising FTZ, signed zero, NaN and Inf -- and I do not think a Q1 referee rejects for its absence once the limitation is stated.
